root.title: With a Little Help
root.gist: Across these stories, technology that promises control—watches, chips, bots, constitutions—ends up exposing how fragile human trust and self-discipline really are.
root.question: Technology and power — how do surveillance and automation reshape trust between people? (four stories)

children.title: Power Punctuation!
children.gist: A naive truck driver rises through a surveillance-driven corporation, only to discover that the boss's power is itself an illusion passed down a chain of nobodies.
children.question: Power Punctuation — what does Jasper's rise reveal about who is actually in charge? (an epistolary story)

children.title: Meeting Rhindquist
children.gist: Jasper's paranoid roommate Tony distrusts the watches and plugs that track workers, and Jasper's first day on a new truck route introduces him to the eccentric pusher Rhindquist, whom he first mistakes for a spy.

children.title: Becoming Management
children.gist: Jasper is promoted to Special Vice President by Rhindquist, gains new freedoms and office privileges, and spots his old roommate Tony working quietly in the same building's basement.

children.title: Tony's Paranoia
children.gist: Tony, now Jasper's assistant, argues that performance reviews are meaningless and that unseen Ones In Charge secretly run every company, a claim Jasper angrily dismisses as nonsense.

children.title: Power Words and Private Talk
children.gist: Jasper learns impressive-sounding Power Words and finally asks Rhindquist directly whether he truly runs the company, hearing instead a surprisingly ordinary account of lucky, violent beginnings.

children.title: A Day Without the Watch
children.gist: Freed from his usual truck watch's constant praise, Jasper complains to a maintenance operator about being micromanaged by machines, revealing how normalized constant feedback has become.

children.title: The Microsoft Crisis
children.gist: Left in charge of the office, Jasper snoops through confidential files, fixes his cousin's unjust imprisonment, then unwittingly authorizes a violent strike against a rival city while filling in for Rhindquist.

children.title: Breakdown and Confession
children.gist: Horrified by the violence he unknowingly caused, Jasper collapses into despair, and Rhindquist admits he engineered Jasper's promotion because he wanted someone to take his own miserable job.

children.title: A New Successor
children.gist: Jasper proposes that Tony, who already distrusts the system, should become the new frontman, and Rhindquist happily agrees, completing the cycle of passing power to the next unwitting puppet.

children.title: Afterword
children.gist: A short author's note on the story's origin and sale.

children.title: Visit the Sins
children.gist: A graduate student interviews his surgically-altered grandfather about a chip that lets people switch off from boring life, confronting how escape from discomfort can hollow out relationships.
children.question: Visit the Sins — why do people choose to switch themselves off from life? (a family confrontation)

children.title: The Thesis Begins
children.gist: Sean travels to Florida to secretly interview his institutionalized grandfather for a thesis on generational avoidance, without telling his estranged father about the visit.

children.title: First Encounter on the Ward
children.gist: Sean finds Grampa in a passive maintenance mode among other surgically altered patients, remembering how violently intelligent and cruel Grampa became whenever he was fully switched on.

children.title: The First Interview
children.gist: Sean questions Grampa about his wealth, his switched-off reflex, and whether his father wishes him dead, provoking Grampa into an aggressive, half-convincing defense of his own behavior.

children.title: Wealth and Reflex
children.gist: Grampa insists switching off is an uncontrollable reflex everyone shares, while Sean counters that it is a learned habit of avoidance that Grampa alone indulges without restraint.

children.title: Does He Resent You
children.gist: Pressed on his father's feelings, Grampa deflects into legal and financial offers, exposing how he mistakes material generosity for genuine emotional repair with his estranged son.

children.title: Visits and Sleep
children.gist: Grampa admits his father visits monthly only to force him switched on, and describes switching off as unlike sleep, an absence he does not experience as frustrating.

children.title: End of the First Day
children.gist: The noisy ward ruins Sean's recording, so he retreats to a run-down motel and meets Adele, another visitor devoted to her own institutionalized, mostly switched-off son.

children.title: Adele's Story
children.gist: By the motel pool, Adele cheerfully describes her son Ethan's childhood surgery and current detachment, refusing to see how little of him remains present when he is switched off.

children.title: Day Two with Ethan
children.gist: Sean introduces Adele's son Ethan to Grampa, then confronts Grampa with logfile evidence proving he chose to switch off during his own son's childhood rather than being powerless to stop it.
children.question: Day two — can logfiles prove that switching off was always a choice, not a reflex? (a confrontation)

children.title: Introducing Ethan
children.gist: Adele brings her son Ethan to meet Grampa, hoping the two detached old men will become friends, while Sean watches with disgust at their empty, mechanical politeness.

children.title: Confronting the Logfiles
children.gist: Sean reveals he has Grampa's logfiles showing he rarely switched off at work but used it heavily during family time, undercutting Grampa's claim that switching off is beyond his control.

children.title: Marriage and Divorce
children.gist: Grampa recounts enjoying his ex-wife's preference for his switched-off self, while Sean reveals his own failed relationship collapsed for eerily similar reasons of inattentiveness and cruelty.

children.title: The Visitation Argument
children.gist: Sean forces Grampa to admit, logfile by logfile, that he stayed switched off through his son's childhood visitations, a fact Grampa still refuses to accept as neglect.

children.title: Three Generations at the Table
children.gist: Ethan and Grampa answer Adele's chatter with identical mechanical yeses, foreshadowing Sean's father's imminent, unannounced visit to the ward the next morning.

children.title: Leaving the Ward
children.gist: After leaving Grampa and Ethan together, Sean confronts Adele at the pool, insisting that her switched-off son is no longer really present, a truth she refuses to accept.
children.question: Leaving the ward — can loved ones accept that a switched-off person is effectively gone? (no settled answer)

children.title: A Grin and a Question
children.gist: Sean imagines Grampa and Ethan trading empty maintenance-mode pleasantries, then asks Adele why she ever agreed to institutionalize her son in the first place.

children.title: Only Subroutines Left
children.gist: Sean angrily tells Adele that Ethan and Grampa are essentially gone, reduced to subroutines, but Adele refuses the idea and sends him off to cool down alone.

children.title: The Father Arrives
children.gist: Sean drives Adele to collect his estranged father from the airport, needling him about generational cowardice while Adele innocently proposes a cheerful family outing to Universal Studios.
children.question: The airport — can Sean provoke his father into admitting his own avoidance? (a car-ride confrontation)

children.title: Driving to the Airport
children.gist: Sean nurses a hangover while driving Adele to meet his father, and Adele unknowingly predicts that visiting an amusement park could keep the detached old men switched on longer.

children.title: Confronting His Father
children.gist: In the car, Sean needles his withdrawn father about needing deliberate effort to switch off unlike Grampa, provoking silent, wounded discomfort instead of the usual sharp rebuttal.

children.title: The Reunion
children.gist: At the ward, three generations clash over blame and weakness until Ethan's outburst shatters Sean's father's composure, leaving Sean guilty for finally breaking the distance he wanted to expose.
children.question: The reunion — what happens when three generations finally say what switching off has cost them? (a family showdown)

children.title: Arriving at the Table
children.gist: Sean introduces his father to Adele and Grampa, baiting him about needing special effort to stay emotionally present, while his father's guarded composure begins visibly to crack.

children.title: Questions and Outbursts
children.gist: Pressed by Sean's pointed questions, Ethan erupts defending the pleasure of switching off, and Grampa coldly dismisses any responsibility for the pain his detachment caused his son.

children.title: Father Walks Away
children.gist: Sean's father, visibly wounded by Grampa's cruelty, excuses himself with forced dignity, leaving Sean to invite Adele and Ethan to Universal Studios instead, uncertain if kindness can undo the damage.

children.title: Afterword
children.gist: A personal note on the author's own family experience with dementia inspiring the story.
